what_happened: The task description's quoted yield (17 valid of 806 at complexity 4 over Base) counts 15 structural-prefilter decisions that carry no derivation at all; only 2 of the 17 have a proof_trace. The theorem-half yield of the tableau proper is ~12% of the headline valid_count (c4 2/17, c5 8/100, c6 42/790).

TheoremEntry.proof requires a DerivationTree schematic in all arguments, but no Formula-to-Formula uniform substitution exists as data anywhere in the tree -- only the L-to-L-plus substPlus/PlusDerivationTree.ofTMSubst. The ADMIT stage cannot be built without an L-level DerivationTree.subst.

Compile-verified that the missing L-level uniform substitution is a mechanical port of PlusDerivationTree.ofTMSubst: substF, Axiom.ofSubst (20 arms), Axiom.minFrameClass_ofSubst, substF_reflectTime and DerivationTree.subst all elaborate sorry-free, and register_theorem ACCEPTS a row built by generalizing a concrete derivation (profile box, arity 1, fragment ModalBoolean; axioms propext+Quot.sound).

scripts/proof-mode-cost-baseline.sh pins a measured surface that INCLUDES the directory BimodalLib/Diagnostics. Adding the five reserved-stage emitters there moves the surface head and makes the cost baseline stale: verified exit 3 ('STALE BASELINE') with a deliberately wrong --pin. Either site the new emitters outside that directory or narrow SURFACE to the three measured files.

Proof extraction is Base-only: extractProof ignores its frame-class argument (_fc) and ProofExtractionResult.success is hard-coded to DerivationTree .Base. So the description's 'at each frame class the tableau accepts' buys nothing on the theorem half; stronger classes change only which branches close, i.e. the countermodel half.

Two complexity-4 dataset artifacts disagree on the valid count: data/bmlogic-c4_metadata.json reports 17 valid / 669 invalid / 120 undetermined of 806, data/exhaustive_c4_metadata.json reports 13 / 673 / 120. Whichever figure the record quotes must name its artifact.

The gate-pass-rate probe (enumerate at bound 4, decide at Base and ZTime, evaluate the eight gates per invalid verdict) did not finish in 25 minutes and was stopped. evalBranchGates re-runs buildTableau for every invalid verdict, roughly doubling DECIDE cost; the per-cell gate pass rate is unmeasured and is the first figure the plan's opening phase should take.

Two copies of the gate-pass-rate probe ran concurrently for ~20 minutes. The first launch call failed on its PID-file write (an unquoted scratchpad variable resolved to /yield.pid, Permission denied) but had ALREADY backgrounded the lean job, so the relaunch added a second elaboration competing for the same cores; and killing the recorded PID only killed the subshell, leaving the timeout/lake/lean children alive. Both instances were found via pgrep and killed. Lesson: quote the scratchpad path variable, and kill the process GROUP or the timeout wrapper's own PID, not the subshell's.

Research report's compiled probe had already elaborated the full five-declaration L-level substitution construction AND run register_theorem on a generalized row, so the plan's critical-path phase is authored against a verified shape rather than a hypothesis.

readme-lint.sh Check 4's grandfathering is asymmetric and is NOT in context/project/lean4/patterns/plan-authoring-gate-collisions.md: BimodalTools/README.md (stale 2026-09-27), FormalSystem/README.md (stale 2026-10-02) and FormalSystem/ProofSystem/README.md (stale 2026-09-21) are pinned in scripts/readme-date-baseline.txt, so refreshing their Last-verified stamps UN-grandfathers them and fails the gate, while BimodalLib/README.md and BimodalLib/Theorems/README.md carry no baseline row and therefore MUST be refreshed on touch. Planned per-phase accordingly.

typst/generated/status.typ counts FormalSystem/, Tests/ and BimodalTools/ .lean lines but NOT BimodalLib/ (scripts/typst-status-counts.sh:202-207), while .githooks/pre-commit fires on any staged .lean path. A phase touching only BimodalLib/** therefore needs no status.typ regeneration; every phase touching FormalSystem/, BimodalTools/ or Tests/ does, commit-blocking.

Reading extractProof live showed its strategies (tryAxiomProof, matchDerived, buildCompositionalProof, enhancedSearch) are pure functions of the formula alone, with the tableau only gating the .allClosed branch. That opened a second admission route (elaboration-time extraction) which the plan then deliberately rejected in favour of source emission, on the ground that no native_decide is available and the kernel would have to reduce bounded proof search. The alternative is recorded as a Decision so it is not rediscovered mid-implementation.

Carried-figure discipline run at dispatch 6 start: all four figures from the dispatch description confirmed live. data/bmlogic-c4_metadata.json still reports total_records=806, valid_count=17, invalid_count=669, timeout_count=120, frame_class=Base, and decision_method_distribution.structural_prefilter=15 (so the derivation-bearing yield is 17-15=2, the plan's material qualification holds). not_valid_of_hasOpen_int is live at IntTruth.lean:1045. ProofExtractionResult.success is still hard-coded to DerivationTree .Base [] phi (ProofExtraction.lean:238), so the theorem half remains Base-only.

Phase 1 probe's gate_ms column is contaminated and must not be read as the marginal cost of gating. The per-gate histogram accumulates Nat fields inside a List.foldl (h.timeOrderTotal + b g.timeOrderTotal), which Lean builds as a thunk chain; the IO.monoMsNow window around the fold therefore measures thunk construction only, and every Base row reported 0 ms while the real tableau rebuild cost is paid when the row is printed. The gate PASS-RATE figures (per-gate counts and GATED) are unaffected and valid, since printing forces them. The marginal-cost figure needs a separate measurement that forces the accumulator before stopping the clock.

CORRECTION to the earlier gate_ms issue entry for this dispatch: the lazy-accumulation diagnosis was wrong and is withdrawn. The DECIDE stage uses the identical List.foldl-over-a-Nat-structure shape and reported a nonzero 35 ms / 38252 ms, so the fold is strict and the timed window does capture the tableau rebuilds. gate_ms=0 at Base is therefore a REAL measurement, not an artifact. The actual finding is that gating cost is wildly asymmetric across frame classes: negligible at Base, and so expensive at Dense that four ModalBoolean gate rows did not finish in nine minutes of wall clock. That asymmetry, not a timing bug, is the Phase 6 input.

The plan's Phase 1 mitigation for timing contamination -- take the measurement once under the shared .lake/build-guard.lock -- is INSUFFICIENT, and this dispatch measured why. That lock serializes lake invocations only. The actual contention source during this run was a sibling dispatch's 'run-all.sh --jobs auto' shell test sweep over ~120 suites (pid 2935696) plus several concurrent claude processes, none of which take the lake lock: load average 6.45 on 24 cores. ModalBoolean's DECIDE stage took 38s on the first run and had not finished after 5.5 minutes on the second, identical run. CONSEQUENCE: under a multi-task /orchestrate batch, no wall-clock figure from this probe may be presented as uncontended. The COUNT figures (per-gate histograms, four-way decision splits, enumeration yields) are contention-independent and reproduced exactly across both runs, so they stand.
git-commit-scoped.sh dropped 'Tests/BimodalLibTest.lean' from a commit pathspec: not contained in task #972's declared file_scope.

The plan's per-phase 'Files to modify' lists omit the TEST LIBRARY ROOTS (Tests/BimodalLibTest.lean, Tests/BimodalToolsTest.lean) while listing the individual test files under them. A new test file is not in the build at all until its root imports it, so the omission is load-bearing. Because file_scope is harvested from the plan, git-commit-scoped.sh then dropped Tests/BimodalLibTest.lean as out-of-scope and silently committed Phase 3 with the new test orphaned in HEAD -- it built locally only because the working tree had the import. Remedy applied: added both roots to task 972's file_scope via state-write.sh and committed the root separately. Phases 4 and 5 add Tests/BimodalToolsTest/*.lean and will hit the same gap; the root is now in scope for them.

Phase 2's five-declaration L-level uniform substitution (substF, substF_reflectTime, Axiom.ofSubst with 20 arms, Axiom.minFrameClass_ofSubst, DerivationTree.subst with 7 arms, DerivationTree.substNil) compiled clean on the FIRST build with no warnings, because FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/Substitution.lean is an arm-for-arm template at the L-plus level and the plan said to mirror it. #print axioms gives [propext, Quot.sound] for substNil -- no sorryAx, no Classical.choice -- which is exactly what register_theorem accepts. Mirroring an existing verified module beat deriving the proof structure from scratch by a wide margin.

Phase 7's task 'add assert_no_subsumed_entries to BimodalLib/Theorems/Complete.lean, so non-redundancy of the registry becomes a build invariant' cannot be executed as written. The command, landed in Phase 3, reports 26 of the 190 live registry rows as substitution instances of another row, and they are deliberate named laws rather than defects: Combinators.topThm's own proof term is literally 'identity Formula.bot', so it IS Combinators.identity at bot, and Propositional.em unfolds to (A -> bot) -> (A -> bot), an instance of A -> A. Wiring the unscoped command globally would turn the build red on 26 hand-curated entries the reference manual cites. Per .claude/rules/plan-compliance.md this was RAISED rather than silently substituted: the command was landed with assert_registry_complete's own optional prefix argument (the plan told Phase 3 to mirror that elaborator), the unscoped form is implemented and available, and nothing is wired globally, so the build is green under any ruling. user_decision set on .return-meta.json with three options; the scoped form over BimodalLib.Theorems.Enumerated is the recommended default. Phases 4-6 do not need the ruling.

The Phase 1 baseline capture paid for itself twice over in the same dispatch. Both check-module-invariants.sh (C12, C20) and readme-lint.sh (4 new stale dates) are RED in this repo before the task touches anything, so a naive reading of either gate at phase end would have looked like a regression this task caused. Capturing the exact pre-task finding SET, not just the exit code, let Phases 2 and 3 each be discharged by byte-identical reproduction of those findings plus explicit PASSes on the named invariants (INV, B3, C26, C33). The BimodalLib/Diagnostics staleness pin also matched docs/development/proof-mode-cost-baseline.md exactly, confirming Phase 5's siting decision has a clean pin to preserve.
